title: Kausani - Switzerland of India in Uttarakhand
content:
Kausani - Uttarkhand,

Kausani is one of those places in Uttarakhand where time seems to slow down. Perched at around 1,890 meters in the Bageshwar district, this small hill town is best known for its wide-angle views of the Himalayas. On a clear morning, you can spot giants like Nanda Devi, Trishul, and Panchachuli shining in the sunlight, stretching across nearly 300 km of skyline. It’s the kind of sight that stays in your memory long after the trip is over.

Unlike its busy neighbor Nainital, Kausani is quiet, calm, and still carries the charm of an old mountain village. The pace here is slow—locals go about their day tending orchards and fields, while visitors sip hot tea on balconies overlooking the valleys. No honking traffic, no loud crowds - just the sound of birds, rustling pine trees, and the occasional temple bells.

This peaceful setting once inspired Mahatma Gandhi, who spent a few weeks here in 1929. He called Kausani the “Switzerland of India” because of its natural beauty and the way the snow peaks shine like jewels under the sun. His stay is now remembered at the Anashakti Ashram, a simple retreat that still attracts visitors seeking calm and inspiration.

Nature lovers will also enjoy the lush tea gardens around Kausani, where you can walk among neatly lined bushes and even taste the fresh local brew. For a little adventure, there are short treks leading to waterfalls, caves, and quiet villages tucked inside the pine forests.

Whether you want to spend your days reading a book by the window, walking through orchards, watching the sun dip behind the mountains, or exploring local culture, Kausani gives you the perfect setting. It isn’t about ticking off a long list of tourist spots—it’s about slowing down, breathing the crisp mountain air, and letting the Himalayas work their magic on you.

Best Time to Visit Kausani:

  • Peak Season (March - June): Pleasant weather (15°C - 25°C), perfect for sightseeing and treks.
  • Monsoon (July - September): Heavy rainfall, greenery at its best, average 10°C - 20°C. Roads may be slippery.
  • Winter (October - February): Cold with temperatures dropping to 2°C, clear skies for Himalayan views, and chances of light snowfall in December - January.

Location (Distance from City Center):

  • From Almora: 52 km,
  • From Ranikhet: 59 km,
  • From Kathgodam Railway Station: 132 km,
  • From Delhi: Around 420 km (10–11 hrs drive),

Things to Do in Kausani:

  • Visit Anashakti Ashram - Experience peace where Gandhi once stayed.
  • Walk through Tea Gardens - See how tea is grown and processed in Kausani’s famous estates.
  • Enjoy Himalayan Views - Sunrise and sunset from Kausani are unforgettable.
  • Rudradhari Falls & Caves - A scenic trek through pine forests leads to this hidden waterfall.
  • Visit Lakshmi Ashram - A Gandhian educational institute run by women.
  • Shopping for Woolens - Buy handmade shawls, caps, and sweaters at the Kausani Shawl Factory.
  • Trekking & Nature Walks - Explore short treks around the valley for close encounters with nature.

Top 10 Places to Visit Near Kausani (within 50 km):

1- Baijnath Temple (16 km) - Ancient Shiva temple on the banks of Gomti River.

2- Someshwar (12 km) - A religious town with scenic valley views.

3- Binsar (48 km) - Famous for its wildlife sanctuary and panoramic views.

4- Ranikhet (59 km) - A peaceful cantonment town.

5- Almora (52 km) - Known for culture, handicrafts, and local sweets.

6- Bageshwar (38 km) - A town of temples with riverside views.

7- Kapkot (49 km) - A small scenic village surrounded by mountains.

8- Patal Bhuvaneshwar (50 km) - A limestone cave temple full of legends.

9- Chaukori (50 km) - Known for tea gardens and sunrise views.

10- Someshwar Valley (15 km) - Great for scenic drives and photography.
excerpt: Kausani is a peaceful hill station in Uttarakhand, loved for Himalayan views, tea gardens, and Gandhi’s Anashakti Ashram. It’s the perfect escape for nature lovers and those who want calm, slow travel.
